jobs.title: Electrical Engineer
jobs.description:
**About Relling:** Relling (YC S25) builds ready-to-deploy robot workcells for US manufacturers. We design and test in San Francisco and put systems to work on factory floors. This is a full-time, in-person role in Potrero Hill, San Francisco.
  
  
**What you'll do:** Design, build and wire control panels for robotic workcells, from schematics and panel layout through wiring, labeling and documentation. Select and integrate power distribution, motor drives and servo amplifiers, PLCs, safety relays and controllers, sensors, I/O and industrial networks such as EtherCAT and EtherNet/IP. Design wiring harnesses and cable routing for robots and end-of-arm tooling, and design and bring up custom PCBs where off-the-shelf parts fall short. Commission cells on the factory floor, troubleshoot electrical faults under real production conditions, and make sure every system is safe, serviceable and built to code.
  
  
**What we're looking for:** Hands-on experience designing and building electrical systems you can explain end to end, such as control panels, harnesses, power electronics or PCBs. Strong fundamentals in circuits, power, grounding and shielding, and comfort with schematic and layout tools (e.g. EPLAN, AutoCAD Electrical, KiCad or Altium). Familiarity with industrial standards and machine safety (NFPA 79, UL 508A, safety-rated circuits) is a strong plus. A practical approach to debugging: measurements, root causes and validation.
  
  
**How to apply:** Apply with your resume and a short description of an electrical system you built or shipped. Project links are optional. Tell us what you owned, what failed and how you tested the fix.

Reference Image is one of Apple's most ambitious end-to-end security and imaging initiatives: a system that lets users cryptographically verify that a photo genuinely came from an Apple device sensor, unaltered. We're looking for a Systems Engineer to join the Reference Image team and own key pieces of the technical architecture and cross-stack integration, someone who can reason across hardware security, cloud infrastructure, and application-layer behavior. You'll work under the guidance of the project DRI, taking ownership of specific systems-level work streams while helping drive alignment across a distributed, multi-team effort toward a coherent, secure, and shippable system.  
  
**Description**  
  
In this role you’ll be expected to:  
  

* Contribute to and help maintain the systems architecture for Reference Image, spanning sensor-level signing, on-device RAW capture pipelines, and cloud-based development in PCC.

* Work closely with Security and Privacy teams to help threat-model end-to-end media authenticity workflows, evaluating cryptographic integrity, data privacy, and downstream non-destructive edit handling.

  

* Help evaluate and advance standard and extended image container formats to support secure provenance and authenticity metadata.

  

* Coordinate with PCC/Cloud infrastructure teams on specific integration points to ensure the signing and certificate infrastructure scales and meets the security bar.

  

* Represent your work stream's technical tradeoffs in cross-functional forums (Photos, Camera Capture, ISP/hardware, QA, Privacy, Legal, Marketing), proactively identifying and resolving cross-team technical dependencies and blockers.

  

* Contribute to scoping and planning for future hardware generations under the direction of the DRI.

  
**Preferred Qualifications**  
  
Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, still-evolving system with real security stakes and public-facing implications (e.g., newsroom/wire-service use cases).  
  
Capable of coding to fill functional gaps in the team.  
  
Familiarity with trusted time stamping mechanisms and their role in establishing chain-of-custody for signed data.  
  
Experience working on flagship security or trust features that ship across multiple operating systems.  
  
Familiarity with international privacy/regulatory considerations affecting feature availability by region.
